back: Create, Read, Update, Delete: the four basic operations on stored data (INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE in SQL).
A database object for entering, viewing and editing data one record at a time in a user-friendly layout.
A database object that presents data from a table or query in a formatted layout for reading or printing, often grouped with totals.
A row-and-column view of a table or query in which many records can be viewed and edited directly.
UPDATE Table SET Field = value WHERE condition;  (no WHERE = every record changes)

back: INSERT INTO Table VALUES (v1, v2, …);   DELETE FROM Table WHERE condition;
A filter temporarily hides non-matching records in a datasheet; a query is a saved, reusable selection that can feed forms and reports.
Puts records in ascending or descending order of a field; it never changes the stored values.
Drop-down lists (allowed values), check boxes (Yes/No), clear labels, tab order, validation messages, input masks.
